title: Low-bit streaming mux: kernel contracts, KV cache snapshots, and scheduling notes
content:
Overview:

This is a working draft describing a streaming/microbatch multiplexer (mux) approach for low-bit execution paths (INT8, FP8, GPTQ, AWQ). It consolidates kernel contract expectations, KV-cache snapshot semantics, and scheduler heuristics required to support safe, low-latency handoffs between mixed-precision kernels during live inference (streaming responses and continuous KV cache reuse).

Goals:
- Define minimal kernel contract surface for interchangeable low-bit kernels in the streaming/microbatch case.
- Specify KV cache snapshot + patch protocol so dequant/requant and kernel handoffs preserve correctness and minimize copying.
- Surface scheduling heuristics and safety checks to prevent precision mismatch regressions or KV-coherence violations under high concurrency.
- Produce a test-plan and telemetry hooks for rollout and A/B.

Non-goals:
- This doc does not re-specify full operator ABI (separate contract exists). We assume existing kernels implement op-level shapes. Focus here is on cross-kernel state, handshake, and scheduling.

Motivating example:
Incoming streaming request uses cached prefix (from prior chat turn) encoded and stored as INT8-packed KV entries produced by GPTQ transform. New tokens will be generated using an AWQ-int8 kernel for output efficiency, but certain layers have FP8 fallback due to numerical instability at longer contexts. We need a safe handoff that: (1) allows incremental token emission without full re-dequantization, (2) avoids duplicative KV copies across worker threads, and (3) ensures fallback to FP8 or full-precision doesn't corrupt future cache states.

Definitions (used later):
- worker-kernel: a kernel binary that processes one or more transformer layers and understands a precision mode (e.g., int8-awq, gptq-4bit, fp8-epoch2).
- kvcache-entry: serialized KV pair for a single layer/position. Metadata includes precision tag, quant-table id, and commit-sequence.
- microbatch: a scheduling unit smaller than the request; used for streaming token emission.

High-level design principles:
1) Precision-tagged KV entries: every cache entry carries a metadata tuple: {precision, quant-id, version, origin-kernel-id}. The runtime must reject applying a kvcache entry if precision or quant-id is incompatible unless a registered adaptor is available.
2) Lazy patching + view semantics: kernels should be allowed to reference KV entries immutably when their execution path can operate on the packed representation (no dequant). When a kernel needs dequantized tensors, runtime will produce a transient dequant view logically bound to the execution, with copy-on-write semantics to avoid surprises across concurrent requests.
3) Microbatch-aware handshake: before a microbatch is issued to a kernel, the scheduler and kernel perform a handshake to agree on: expected precision, input view types (packed vs dequant), and a commit token that will be used to stamp any produced kvcache writes.
4) Minimal adaptor interfaces: define small adaptor functions for on-the-fly conversions (packed->float32 view, packed->fp8 view, re-quantize-to-int8 with knob). These should be stateless and reference specified quant tables.

Kernel contract (surface area):
- kernel_id: stable short id (string)
- supported_precisions: list of strings (e.g., ["AWQ_INT8", "GPTQ_4BIT", "FP8_E2"])
- requires_dequant_view: boolean (true if kernel expects dequantized tensors)
- produces_packed_kv: boolean (true if kernel writes packed entries)
- kv_write_semantics: enum {append, overwrite, conditional-overwrite} (describes how writes should be applied)
- handshake_api(signature):
    - request_signature = {microbatch_id, expected_precision, input_kv_versions, token_offset}
    - response = {accepted: bool, adaptor_needed: optional(adaptor_id), commit_token}
- rollback_callback(commit_token): invoked by runtime on failed microbatch to clear transient writes

KV cache snapshot & commit protocol:
- Reads: worker kernels may read kvcache entries in-place if supported_precisions contains the entry precision. Reads must be consistent: if microbatch handshake accepts current input_kv_versions, runtime returns a read view bound to the microbatch_id.
- Transient views: if adaptor_needed, runtime creates a transient view (zero-copy when possible) and tags it with microbatch_id. The view has a lifecycle: created->used->released or promoted.
- Writes: kernels acquire a commit_token during handshake. All kvcache writes produced in that microbatch are first staged in a microbatch-local write buffer (staging area). On successful completion, the kernel calls commit(commit_token). Runtime validates that base input_kv_versions have not diverged (if diverged and policy==conditional-overwrite, apply safe merge heuristics). If commit succeeds, staged writes are atomically swapped into the global kvcache (fine-grained per-layer locks).
- Promotion rules: we allow two promotion modes: replace (full overwrite), and merge (layerwise merge preserving newer positions). Merge is used when streaming interleaves writes from multiple producers for the same layer.
- Garbage collection: expired transient views and staging buffers are reclaimed on microbatch completion or after timeout. Long-lived views must be explicitly promoted or discarded.

Scheduler heuristics and safety checks:
- Preferred routing: schedule microbatches to kernels that support the cached precision to avoid adaptor overhead. Node-local preference for cached packed entries to reduce copy.
- Adaptor budget: scheduler maintains a moving window of adaptor CPU and memory usage; prefer routes that keep adaptor usage below threshold.
- Latency SLO guardrails: if adaptor path would increase tail latency above SLO, prefer fallback to a compatible FP8 kernel pre-warmed with dequant views (even if costlier).
- Stale-write detection: before commit, validate input_kv_versions. If mismatch and policy==abort, fail the microbatch and trigger fallback. If mismatch and policy==retry, attempt re-handshake up to N times.
- Fallback cascade: ordered list: same-precision kernel on another node -> FP8 fallback on same node -> scalar (float32) fallback on dedicated node. Cascades should be encoded in runtime policy for customers.

Adaptor / conversion rules:
- Conversions must be deterministic given quant-id and quant-tables. Quant tables are immutable objects with ids; updates produce new quant-ids.
- Conversion cost guidelines: packed->view where no copy possible should be O(1) pointer ops; otherwise provide measured heuristics for copy cost per layer. Runtime telemetry must track adaptor copy rate.

Edge cases and failure modes:
- Concurrent promotion collisions: two microbatches attempt to promote different views for the same layer / same position. Use per-layer commit ordering via commit_token sequence numbers; second committer merges using position-aware merge. If incompatible, second commit fails with merge-conflict telemetry.
- Partial streaming + long prefix retention: when cached prefix spans many layers and is stored mixed across precisions, ensure garbage collection does not reclaim entries still referenced by open streaming sessions. Reference counting or session-scoped GC marker is required.
- Quant-table drift: if a kernel expects quant-id X but input entries are quant-id Y (different scale tables), adaptor required. If no adaptor, abort microbatch and report mismatched-quant telemetry.

Telemetry and rollout plan:
- Emit events for: handshake result (accepted/adaptor-needed/declined), adaptor copy size, commit result (success/merge-conflict/abort), fallback triggered, staging buffer size, microbatch latency breakdown.
- Start with a canary rollout: enable streaming mux for 10% of requests on single region with heavy telemetry. Compare token-latency and merge-conflict rate vs baseline.
- Define safe thresholds for auto-pause: e.g., merge-conflict rate > 0.5% over 1 hour -> disable mixed-precision promotion on live traffic.

Testing and validation plan:
- Unit tests: handshake API permutations, adaptor correctness against gold conversion tool, commit/rollback correctness with mocked kvcache.
- Integration tests: multi-node streaming test that simulates concurrent sessions, interleaved microbatches, and forced quant-id mismatches.
- Load tests: simulated traffic with varying prefix reuse rates to measure adaptor overhead, staging buffer high-water marks, and tail latency.
- Regression metrics: token-per-second improvement, additional CPU cost, proportion of microbatches requiring adaptor.

Open questions / TODOs:
- Decide default commit policy for mixed-precision writes: conditional-overwrite vs append semantics. Propose conditional-overwrite as safe default but may be slower.
- Define precise binary layout for packed KV entries for AWQ and GPTQ to maximize zero-copy view compatibility. Need collaboration with kernel authors.
- Should kernels be allowed to mutate existing packed entries in-place? Current draft forbids in-place mutation unless explicit lock held.
- How to surface customer-level policies for fallback cascades in Console.

Implementation milestones (high-level):
1) Handshake prototype + simple adaptor (Q->float view) and transient view lifecycle (2 weeks)
2) Microbatch commit staging and per-layer atomic swap (3 weeks)
3) Scheduler integration: routing preference and adaptor budget tracking (2 weeks)
4) Canary rollout + telemetry dashboards (1 week)
5) Iteration on merge heuristics and conflict resolution (2 weeks)

Appendix: quick pseudocode for handshake and commit:

// Scheduler issues microbatch
handshake = {microbatch_id, expected_precision, input_kv_versions}
response = kernel.handshake(handshake)
if not response.accepted:
  if response.adaptor_needed:
    view = runtime.make_transient_view(handshake.input_kv)
    if !view: fail microbatch
  else:
    fallback or abort
// kernel executes using view or packed refs, writes to staging
on_success: kernel.commit(response.commit_token)
runtime.commit(commit_token):
  lock layers touched
  if input_kv_versions mismatch and policy==abort:
    unlock layers
    rollback
  apply staged writes (replace or merge)
  release locks

Notes and context:
- This doc intentionally uses coarse-grained language; follow-up PRD will specify exact APIs and wire formats.
- Related docs: runtime kernel ABI, kvcache serialization spec, and scheduler routing policies. See linked_artifacts for immediate references.

Questions for the next sync:
- Kernel authors: can AWQ & GPTQ share identical packed layout for prefix keys? If yes, zero-copy promotions are feasible.
- SRE: what is acceptable staging buffer size per-worker under our P99 tail latency target?
- Product: should customers be allowed to opt-out of mixed-precision promotion at deployment-level?

Author notes (informal):
- I purposefully kept the commit protocol optimistic to favor low-latency streaming. If conflict rates in canary are high we will flip to stricter ordering.
- This draft borrows ideas from previous kvcache commit-stamp and microbatching proposals but emphasizes mixed-precision and zero-copy where possible.

End of draft.
